answer.reason: The ruling shields the former Equilon joint venture's unified pricing from per se Sherman Act liability, a legacy matter since Chevron sold its Equilon stake in 2002. The opinion states no damages figure (the $800 million cost-savings reference is not exposure), the 10-K lists no legal proceedings and does not name the case, and the 10-Q's Equilon indemnity ($300 million maximum) is generic and not tied to this case.
